note: Tornadoes occur out to about 72 h after landfall (rarely up to 5 days). If exponential decay is needed use e-folding ~24-36 h; UNVERIFIED.

label: Storm-total rainfall above which flash/riverine flooding becomes likely in small steep basins
citation: NWS River Forecast Center flash flood guidance concept (1-, 3-, 6-h FFG; steep/urban 1-2 in/h); WPC Excessive Rainfall Outlook is built on exceedance of FFG.
note: UNVERIFIED: no authoritative single storm-total inch threshold found; FFG is basin- and duration-specific. 6 in is a conservative screening value.

label: Near-surface air density in tropical cyclone environment
citation: Ideal gas law: p=1010 hPa, T=28 C, q~22 g/kg gives 1.153 kg/m3 (ISA standard is 1.225).
note: Computed, not from a paper.

label: Environmental pressure
citation: Specified by project; consistent with Holland (1980) outer-pressure convention for the Atlantic.
note: Project convention; Dvorak pairs in wpr_pairs were fit against 1010.

label: Orographic rain coefficient (upslope model)
citation: Smith, R. B., 1979: The influence of mountains on the atmosphere. Adv. Geophys., 21, 87-230 (upslope model P = E·rho·q_s·(U·grad h)); PHRaM topographic term, Lonfat et al. 2007, Mon. Wea. Rev., 135, 3086-3097.
note: Derived, not fitted: c = E·rho·q_s·3600 with precipitation efficiency E = 0.5, air density rho = 1.15 kg/m3 and tropical boundary-layer saturation mixing ratio q_s = 0.018 kg/kg -> 37 mm/h per m/s of forced ascent; capped at 60 mm/h. E is the main uncertainty (0.3-0.9 in the literature); exposed as a lab setting. Terrain slope from a 0.1-degree grid underestimates steep escarpments.
